citation.title: Optimal positive end-expiratory pressure reduces right ventricular dysfunction in COVID-19 patients on venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A retrospective single-center study

provenance.quote: This was a retrospective study of all COVID-19 ECMO patients initiated on VV ECMO from March 2020 through November 2021.
provenance.location: Methods, Study design and setting, para 1

provenance.quote: pressure control ventilation with an inspiratory pressure of 10 cm H2O, PEEP of 10 cm H2O, and a rate of 10 breaths per minute
All patients were hospitalized at OHSU, an academic medical center in Portland, OR with an intensivist-run VV ECMO program
provenance.location: Methods, Study design and setting, para 1

provenance.quote: PEEP was titrated daily using esophageal manometry to an end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure of 0–3 cm H2O throughout the ECMO run

The primary outcome was the incidence of hemodynamically significant RV dysfunction on echocardiogram (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <1.7 cm) requiring inotropic support. Secondary outcomes included ECMO duration, survival to ECMO decannulation, survival to hospital discharge, incidence of barotrauma, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay (LOS).
Of the 69 included patients, 25 were in the standard PEEP group and 44 in the optimal PEEP group.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ARDS: All patients had COVID-19 ARDS on VV ECMO. Obesity: cohort median BMI 39.5 kg/m2, and optimal group median 42.5 kg/m2 (both ≥30). Timing: intervention applied 'throughout the ECMO run' without a specified reference event; unclear if early or late. PtP target: end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure 0–3 cm H2O (absolute positive end-expiratory PtP).

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: Checked COHORTS.md; this report is not listed in any suspected cluster. No trial registration number or overlapping enrolment dates with listed clusters. Single-center retrospective at OHSU; no evidence of overlap with other records.
unclear_items: adults_18_plus: No explicit age criterion stated; inferred adult based on ICU setting. Coded yes.
Continuous variables in Table 1 and Table 3: value_type not specified (mean vs median). Recorded as null.
Balloon calibration method and transpulmonary pressure computation not reported. Coded as not_reported.
timing_subgroup: unclear because reference event for start of intervention not specified (only 'throughout the ECMO run').
extraction_flags.general_notes: This is a retrospective single-center study comparing two time periods (standard PEEP before Jan 2021 vs optimal PEEP after Jan 2021), not a randomized comparison. The optimal PEEP group had higher BMI, more proning on ECMO, and were treated later in the pandemic, all acknowledged as potential confounders.
